title: Runtime kernel candidate pruning and stability playbook
creator: Aisha Khan
root_cause: A recent scheduler heuristic change expanded the candidate kernel set evaluated for each inference request under mid-sized batch depths. In combination with a previously-merged attention micro-optimization that altered cost estimates for fused-attention variants, the scheduler began favoring lower-throughput kernels for a subset of model shapes. This produced increased queuing and KV-cache miss amplification in steady-state bursts, causing 95th/99th latency spikes and degraded throughput on Dedicated hosts. The regression surfaced only under mixed-concurrency workloads and after a hidden interaction with the probe-windowing backoff logic.
postmortem_summary: On 2026-03-08 we observed a sustained latency regression for several customer routes (p95 up ~2.3x, p99 up ~3.7x) correlated with mixed-concurrency traffic patterns. Initial mitigation (force-fallback to pre-change kernel ranking) reduced latency immediately. Root cause analysis identified an interaction between the new scheduler candidate expansion heuristic and a parallel attention micro-optimization that shifted benchmark cost models. This ticket captures the follow-ups: pruning noisy candidate kernels, introducing deterministic candidate scoring, expanding blackbox regression tests, and a short-term runtime guard (node-fence + circuit breaker) to prevent recurrence during canaries and rollouts.
description:
Context:
- Incident window: 2026-03-08 02:14–05:10 UTC (production signals first spike at 02:14).
- Affected surface: Redwood Dedicated inference workers with mixed small/medium sequence workloads (typical customer apps: chat + system prompts with variable lengths).
- Observable symptoms: sudden increase in p95/p99 token latency, CPU-side worker queuing, increased KV-cache misses, and transient reduction in sustained throughput.
- Short-term mitigation already applied: pinned kernel ranking to previous release ordering for paused canaries and emergency rollback for the scheduler heuristic (rollback PR #GH-8092).

What we investigated:
- Scheduler decision traces (request -> candidate list -> score) for affected requests across three hosts.
- Benchmarks comparing cost model estimates pre/post micro-optimization for attention fused kernels.
- Probe windowing logs and backoff counters during the regression window.
- KV cache metrics and eviction rates correlated with kernel switches.

Key findings:
1) Candidate set growth: the heuristic change widened the candidate pool for mid-depth batches to include more quantized and fallback kernels. That increased scheduling entropy and the probability of picking a suboptimal kernel for the observed sequence-length distribution.
2) Cost-estimate skew: the attention micro-optimization changed measured per-token CPU cost for fused-attn vs unfused-attn on some GPUs; the scheduler's estimator was not recalibrated, so scores became biased toward kernels that empirically performed worse for these workloads.
3) Probe/backoff interaction: probe-windowing backoff intended to damp probing of new kernels allowed some noisy switches to persist longer than expected during bursts, amplifying KV-cache warmup costs and raising latencies.
4) Canary coverage gap: our canary matrix did not include the specific mixed-concurrency profile that triggered the regression, so the change passed rollout checks.
steps_taken: 2026-03-08 03:05 UTC — Emergency rollback of scheduler heuristic (PR GH-8092) which immediately reduced p95~ to baseline for affected routes.
2026-03-08 03:40 UTC — Temporary config: enforce deterministic kernel ranking for Dedicated hosts serving flagged customer routes via feature-flag 'stable-kernel-ranking'.
2026-03-09 10:20 UTC — Deployed node-level circuit breaker to suppress candidate expansion when probe success rate < 60% for a 5-minute window (runtime guard implemented GH-8145).
2026-03-10 14:00 UTC — Replayed representative production traces in staging and validated fixes on heterogenous GPU types (A10 + A100 mix).
action_items: A1: Implement candidate-pruning rules in scheduler to cap candidate set size per request shape; owner Marcus Lee; estimate 3 pts; due 2026-03-21; PR target GH-8210.

A2: Add deterministic scoring layer: produce stable tiebreaker using request-hash + host-stable-seed to avoid non-deterministic kernel oscillation; owner Priya Patel; estimate 3 pts; due 2026-03-18; will be gated behind feature-flag 'deterministic-kernel-score'.

A3: Recalibrate cost models for attention micro-optimizations across supported GPU SKUs and include cost-estimate validation in the CI perf job; owner Daniel Wu; estimate 5 pts; due 2026-03-25; dashboard GH-issues linked in comments.

A4: Expand canary test matrix: add mixed-concurrency profiles, variable-length chat workloads, and KV-cache-warmup scenarios to automated canaries; owner SRE team (lead: Nina Gomez); estimate 5 pts; due 2026-04-01.
A5: Create runtime guard 'node-fence' policy to prevent candidate expansion when observed probe volatility > threshold; owner Marcus Lee; estimate 2 pts; due 2026-03-17.

A6: Post-deploy observability: instrument per-request candidate-trajectory traces and add alerting for 'kernel flip rate' > 0.2 flips/sec per worker; owner Observability team (lead: Omar Ruiz); estimate 2 pts; due 2026-03-20.
A7: Write regression test harness that replays anonymized 2-week production traces with injected concurrency bursts; owner QA (lead: Leah Chen); estimate 4 pts; due 2026-03-29.
A8: Customer-facing follow-up: outreach to affected customers with summary and mitigation timeline; owner CSM: Elena Marin; due 2026-03-15.
risks_and_open_questions: RQ1: Candidate-pruning thresholds may reduce overall throughput for certain niche shapes; need microbenchmarks across 50+ shapes to tune safely.
RQ2: Deterministic scoring could hide genuine improvements if the tiebreaker is too aggressive; will require an A/B window to validate quality and latency impact.
RQ3: Cost-estimate recalibration requires representative hardware in CI; procurment lead to confirm access to A10 and older SKUs for validation.

RQ4: How to represent 'probe volatility' as a stable metric across hosts with different baseline noise? Define probe_volatility = moving-std(candidate_pick_rate) over 1m window and validate signal fidelity.
